standard: course-sentence-translation 技能 R1–R4；键取自对齐原串

entries.en: Old Wives’ Tales are those ‘helpful’ things that your grandparents say that are probably not true.
entries.zh: “老妇人故事”是祖父母们常说的那些“有用”的话，但它们可能并不是真的。

entries.en: They are things like, ‘If you watch a lot of TV, you’ll get square eyes’, ‘If you eat carrots, you’ll see well in the dark’, or ‘If you eat cheese at night, you’ll have bad dreams’.
entries.zh: 它们就像：“如果你看太多电视，眼睛会变成方的”“如果你吃胡萝卜，你在黑暗里也能看得很清楚”，或者“如果你晚上吃奶酪，会做噩梦”。

entries.en: But are they nonsense or is there sometimes a little bit of truth in them?
entries.zh: 但它们是胡说八道，还是有时候也有一点道理？

entries.en: We decided to investigate more.
entries.zh: 我们决定多调查一下。

entries.en: Let’s start with a famous one: ‘An apple a day keeps the doctor away’.
entries.zh: 先从一个很有名的说法说起：“一天一苹果，医生远离我”。

entries.en: My grandma said this all the time.
entries.zh: 我奶奶总是这么说。

entries.en: Well, of course everyone knows that fruit is an important part of a healthy diet.
entries.zh: 当然，大家都知道水果是健康饮食的重要部分。

entries.en: But can one apple really make a difference?
entries.zh: 但一个苹果真的能起作用吗？

entries.en: A medical study from 2013 says ‘yes’.
entries.zh: 2013 年的一项医学研究说是“有”。

entries.en: It found that if people over 50 eat an apple a day, their chances of a heart attack are much smaller than people who don’t.
entries.zh: 研究发现，如果 50 岁以上的人每天吃一个苹果，他们得心脏病的几率比不吃的人小得多。

entries.en: What about ‘Gain a child, lose a tooth’?
entries.zh: 那“生一个孩子，掉一颗牙”呢？

entries.en: They say that when a woman has a child, a tooth will fall out.
entries.zh: 他们说，女人生一个孩子，就会掉一颗牙。

entries.en: Researchers at the New York University College of Dentistry studied more than 2,600 women between the ages of 18 and 64 with one or more children.
entries.zh: 纽约大学牙科学院的研究人员研究了 2,600 多名 18 到 64 岁、有一个或多个孩子的女性。

entries.en: And guess what?
entries.zh: 你猜怎么着？

entries.en: They found they had more problems with their teeth than women with no children, although they couldn’t say exactly why.
entries.zh: 他们发现，这些女性的牙齿问题比没有孩子的女性更多，虽然他们说不出确切原因。

entries.en: My great uncle was a big believer that ‘fish is brain food’.
entries.zh: 我的曾叔叔非常相信“鱼是健脑食物”。

entries.en: He ate it all the time and he was a clever man, too.
entries.zh: 他经常吃鱼，而且他也很聪明。

entries.en: It looks like he might be right.
entries.zh: 看起来他可能是对的。

entries.en: Fish have a lot of omega-3 and omega-6 fats in their oil.
entries.zh: 鱼油里含有很多 omega-3 和 omega-6 脂肪。

entries.en: Some scientists from Oxford studied 120 primary school children, and they discovered that the children who ate omega-3 and omega-6 made big improvements in their schoolwork.
entries.zh: 牛津大学的一些科学家研究了 120 名小学生，发现吃 omega-3 和 omega-6 的孩子在学业上进步很大。

entries.en: If you eat fish oil, it will help to prevent heart problems, too.
entries.zh: 如果你吃鱼油，它也有助于预防心脏问题。

entries.en: It seems like eating fish is a good idea.
entries.zh: 看起来吃鱼是个好主意。

entries.en: Finally, what about those carrots?
entries.zh: 最后，那些胡萝卜呢？

entries.en: Can they really help your night vision?
entries.zh: 它们真的能改善夜间视力吗？

entries.en: I’ve eaten them all my life, but I still walk into things when I get up in the night.
entries.zh: 我一辈子都在吃胡萝卜，但夜里起床时还是会撞到东西。

entries.en: Unfortunately, I can’t find anything to prove if this is right or wrong.
entries.zh: 遗憾的是，我找不到任何证据证明它是对还是错。

entries.en: I’ll keep looking and I’ll let you know as soon as I find out.
entries.zh: 我会继续找，一有发现就告诉你。
